harness: criterion (release build, single seed per case)
notes: psumtree = inline Fenwick BIT with binary-lifting prefix-search; both `set` and `search` are O(log n).

Each step does at most (m + window_expiry) point updates in psumtree plus m O(log n) searches. Edges added at step (i - time_window) are popped from a VecDeque<Option<u32>> history queue and refreshed (their recent in-degree decremented and weight recomputed via pow(new_degree, power) + zero_appeal).

Total cost is O(n * m * log n) for the random walk + O(n * m) amortized for window expiry + O(n*m) for the batched edge insert. Edge insert uses `Graph::add_edges` (one rebuild_indexes call) — never per-call `add_edge` (O(m^2) trap).

Compared to ALGO-GN-018 lastcit at n=5000 (1.65 ms for eps=3), recent_degree at n=5000 (m=3) runs at 2.02 ms — slightly slower because the window-expiry path runs a VecDeque pop + psumtree refresh on every step, whereas lastcit's age sweep only fires at bin boundaries. Both are still O(n log n) and dominate over the legacy O(n^2) cumsum approach.

window_count/n1000_m2 shows mild slowdown (196µs → 216µs, ~10%) going from window=2 to window=200. With window=2 the BIT-tree stays at ~2 hot entries on average; with window=200 it can reach ~200, but log2(200) is still only ~8 — the psumtree's O(log n) per-op cost amortizes the window growth.
m_count/n1000 confirms linear scaling in m: 1→4→16 yields ~79µs / ~432µs / ~1271µs — a factor of ~5x and ~3x per 4x step, dominated by the per-citation psumtree.search cost.
